question: Describe the main properties of electromagnetic waves. Your answer should include their source, need of medium, direction of fields, speed in vacuum, and energy transport.

options.A: Electromagnetic waves are produced by charges at rest and require a material medium. Their electric and magnetic fields are parallel to each other and to the direction of propagation. Their speed in vacuum is variable, and they carry no energy.
options.B:
Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated charges, which create time-varying electric and magnetic fields.
They require no material medium and can travel through vacuum.
The electric and magnetic fields are mutually perpendicular and both are perpendicular to the direction of propagation, so the waves are transverse.
Their speed in vacuum is $c=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}}\approx3.0\times10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
They transport energy, shared between electric and magnetic fields, and also carry momentum.
options.C: Electromagnetic waves are produced by uniformly moving charges and need a medium. Their electric field is parallel to propagation while the magnetic field is absent. They move in vacuum with speed $\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}$ and transport only magnetic energy.
options.D: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated charges and can travel in vacuum. Their electric and magnetic fields are parallel to each other but perpendicular to propagation. Their speed is $3.0\times10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and they carry energy but no momentum.
